metaDescription: Five Beatbot cordless pool robots compared: Sora 10, 30 and 70 plus AquaSense 2 and 2 Ultra, with runtime, surface cleaning and upkeep explained.
expertTake: The Sora 10 is the pick for most owners because it keeps the long battery and waterline reach while skipping the surface skimming extras. The Sora 70 is the value pick only for pools that collect floating debris, and anyone with a plain, clean pool should skip the camera-equipped models.
introParagraphs: One maker's cordless robots can look nearly identical on a shopping page, yet they differ in what part of the pool they actually clean. Some stay on the floor and walls, some add a waterline scrub, and a few also skim the surface.

Choosing within a single brand is mostly about matching the extra feature to the debris you actually have. Pay for surface cleaning only if leaves and pollen float; pay for camera mapping only if your pool has a complicated layout.

products.name: Beatbot Sora 10 cordless, 300-minute battery

specList.label: Shallow areas
specList.value: Handles a shallow platform about 12 inches deep

specList.label: Retrieval
specList.value: Rises to the surface for pickup

products.description:
Start with the battery: a 7,800 mAh pack and a maker-stated 300 minutes make the Sora 10 the endurance model of the lineup short of the Sora 70. That window is long enough for a full pass on a typical residential pool and some margin for a dirty day. The HydroBalance structure is the maker's term for a body layout that keeps weight and water flow balanced against walls.

It skips the surface skimming of the Sora 70, so floating leaves are not its job. Beside the Sora 30, the Sora 10 gives up the fourth cleaning zone but keeps nearly all the practical value, which is why it is the sensible default. Shallow-water cleaning to roughly twelve inches covers a tanning ledge, something many robots simply avoid.

Plan on a charge after each cycle and a rinse of the filter basket, ideally before the sun dries the mesh solid. As with any lithium robot, heat is the enemy, so leave it shaded between runs. Expect the capacity to settle lower after a couple of busy seasons, so the three-hundred-minute figure should be treated as a new-battery number. If the pool sits under a tree line, run it more often for shorter spans instead of one marathon cycle, because a half-full basket cleans better than a packed one. Owners with children should also confirm the lid latches shut after each rinse, since a loose filter door is the usual cause of debris leaking back into the pool.
products.bestFor: Owners of an average in-ground pool who want the best balance of runtime and cost.
pros: Long battery window leaves headroom on dirty days
Handles a shallow ledge many robots avoid
Waterline cleaning included without surface add-ons
Surface pickup spares you from hauling the cable
cons: No surface skimming for floating leaves or pollen
Battery capacity declines after several seasons
Pump rating is not a cleaning guarantee

products.name: Beatbot Sora 30 with platform cleaning
products.description:
The Sora 30 adds a fourth zone, a sun shelf or platform, to the floor, wall and waterline coverage you get elsewhere in the family. Ultrasonic sensors let it detect shallow water instead of stranding itself on a ledge. For pools with a built-in lounge area this is the feature that justifies stepping above the Sora 10.

The tradeoff is that the extra capability is useless in a plain deep pool. Next to the AquaSense 2, which scrubs the waterline twice per pass, the Sora 30 focuses on geometry rather than waterline thoroughness. A pool with a platform and a clean surface is its natural home.

Keep the ultrasonic sensors wipe-clean, since sunscreen film can confuse them. One-touch surface parking means retrieval is easy, but check the app link before relying on it every run. Charge after use and rinse the basket promptly. Because the platform pass adds time to every cycle, schedule it for cooler hours, when the battery runs best. If the shelf is only a few inches deep, watch the first run and confirm the robot turns cleanly at the edge rather than climbing out.
products.bestFor: Pools with a sun shelf, tanning ledge or shallow lounge area.
pros: Fourth zone cleans platforms that others skip
Ultrasonic sensing keeps it from stranding on ledges
Same strong pump rating as the Sora 10
One-touch recall brings it to the surface
cons: Platform cleaning is wasted on a plain deep pool
Costs more than the Sora 10 for a narrow advantage
Sensors need occasional wiping to stay accurate

products.name: Beatbot Sora 70 with JetPulse surface cleaning

specList.label: Surface system
specList.value: JetPulse dual water jets push debris inward

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Surface, waterline, floor, walls, shallow areas

products.description:
This is the only model here that works the water surface. Its JetPulse system uses two jets to create flow that carries floating debris toward the machine, a different mechanism from the floor suction in every other Beatbot. If pollen, blossoms or leaves ride the surface for hours before sinking, this is the robot that grabs them early.

The cost is complexity and price. It sits at the top of the family in cost, and the surface mode drains the battery faster than floor mode, so the five-hour figure applies to floor cleaning. Against the Sora 10, it is a specialist: unless floating debris is your pain point, the Sora 10 delivers most of the benefit for less.

Maintenance has one extra wrinkle. The surface intake and jets must stay unblocked, so inspect them after leafy runs. Each cycle, rinse the filter basket, charge afterward, and avoid leaving the battery in a hot enclosure. Because it is the heaviest and most feature-packed model here, plan a storage spot where it can drain fully and dry before the next run. A damp machine closed in a box invites odor and slow corrosion at the contacts.
products.bestFor: Pools under trees where leaves and pollen sit on top of the water.
pros: Surface jets collect floating debris before it sinks
Largest battery in the family at ten thousand mAh
Covers surface, waterline, floor and walls in one product
AI navigation reduces repeated passes
cons: Most expensive Beatbot in this guide
Surface mode shortens runtime compared with floor mode
More parts to inspect for blockages

products.name: Beatbot AquaSense 2 with double-pass waterline

specList.label: Waterline
specList.value: Scrubs the waterline twice per pass

specList.label: Retrieval
specList.value: Parks at the surface, app recall

products.description:
The AquaSense 2 is the older design in this lineup, built around an unusual idea: scrub the waterline twice during a single pass. That targets the greasy ring where sunscreen and body oils collect, an area most robots touch once and leave. It is less about power than about repeat contact where dirt builds up.

Its calling card on the listing is a three-year protection plan with full machine replacement, which is a stronger ownership promise than most competitors make. Compared with the Sora 10 it has shorter stated endurance, so it fits smaller pools. The surface parking and app recall keep retrieval easy.

Check the protection terms before buying, because replacement policies carry conditions. Rinse the filter each run, keep the battery shaded, and register the machine on day one. The waterline brush is the part to inspect each season, because it does double the work of a single-pass design and wears sooner. Stored upright on a shelf out of the sun, the body should last as long as any plastic pool equipment. If a brush kit is not sold separately, ask the seller before you commit.
products.bestFor: Smaller pools where the waterline ring is the main complaint.
pros: Double-pass waterline scrub targets the scum ring
Three-year protection with machine replacement
Surface parking and app recall ease retrieval
Priced below the newer Sora models
cons: Shorter stated runtime suits smaller pools
Protection plan has terms worth reading
No surface skimming or platform mode

products.name: Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra with AI camera

specList.label: Vision
specList.value: AI camera for mapping and obstacles

products.description:
A camera is the headline of the AquaSense 2 Ultra. It maps the pool, spots obstacles and tells plant debris from other dirt, which helps in a pool with multiple levels, islands or odd cutouts. It is the model to pick when a simpler robot would repeatedly miss corners.

The caddy that ships with it is practical: a loaded robot is heavy and the caddy turns lifting into rolling. The downside is that cameras need clean lenses and decent water clarity, so a murky pool undermines the mapping. Where the Sora 30 relies on ultrasonic sensing, the Ultra is the more capable and more expensive option.

Wipe the camera window after each run and keep the caddy handy for storage. The battery and filter follow the usual cordless routine. Keep expectations modest on water clarity; vision systems degrade when the pool turns cloudy. After a storm or a shock treatment, give the water a day to clear before sending it in, otherwise the mapping may skip areas. Remember that a camera adds one more part that can fail, so factor in the replacement policy before you pay the premium.
products.bestFor: Multi-level or irregular pools that defeat simple navigation.
pros: AI camera maps complex layouts and obstacles
Plant debris recognition adapts the cleaning pattern
Included caddy makes lifting and storage manageable
Handles multi-level pools with platforms
cons: Camera needs clean lens and clear water to work well
Priced at the premium tier of the family

buyingCriteria.explanation: Beatbot labels models by zones: floor, wall, waterline, platform and surface. The Sora 10 covers three, the Sora 30 adds a platform, and the Sora 70 adds surface skimming. Pay only for zones your pool has, and write down which surfaces annoy you today before you shop. A pool without a shelf gains nothing from the platform mode, and a pool without trees gains little from skimming.

The Sora 10 lists up to 300 minutes and the Sora 70 up to five hours on the floor. The AquaSense 2 sits lower. A robot that parks mid-job leaves dirt behind. Size the battery to your pool plus a margin for dirty days.

Only the Sora 70 works the water surface through its JetPulse jets. Floor-suction robots never catch floating debris, which eventually sinks and clogs them. If your pool collects leaves or pollen on top, surface cleaning is worth paying for. If not, skip it.

The AquaSense 2 Ultra uses an AI camera, while the Sora 30 uses ultrasonic sensing for shallow areas. Cameras map better but need clean lenses and clear water. Sensors are simpler and more forgiving. Match the technology to the pool layout and to how clear you keep the water all season.

The AquaSense 2 lists three years of protection with machine replacement. Battery-powered robots wear out, so long coverage matters. Read the terms for conditions, such as registration and proper storage. Coverage is only as good as its fine print.

Wet robots are heavy and the AquaSense 2 Ultra includes a caddy for that reason. Surface parking on the Sora family lets the robot come to you. If lifting is hard for you, rank retrieval above raw specs. A caddy is not a gimmick, and neither is a recall button on a hot afternoon.

specDecoder.meaning: The maker's name for the body layout balancing weight and water flow so the robot stays against walls. It is a design claim, not a measurable spec.
specDecoder.watchFor: Sora 10, Sora 30 and Sora 70 share the idea, so do not treat it as a differentiator.

specDecoder.meaning: A pump flow rating for the impeller. It shows motor strength, not how much dirt leaves the pool.
specDecoder.watchFor: Sora 10 and Sora 30 both quote 6,800 GPH, so choose between them on features, not suction.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery size in milliamp-hours. Bigger means longer cleaning, all else equal.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Sora 70 lists 10,000 mAh against 7,800 mAh on the Sora 10.

specDecoder.meaning: Two water jets that create surface flow to push floating debris inward. It is how the Sora 70 skims.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Sora 70 has it, so the others cannot clean the surface.

specDecoder.meaning: Sound-based distance sensing used to detect shallow water and walls. It works in cloudy water better than vision.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Sora 30 relies on it for platform cleaning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Zone coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We listed which surfaces each robot claims to clean. The Sora 70 covers the most, including the surface. We treated the maker's zone claims as claims, not results.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared mAh and stated minutes across the family. The Sora 10 at 300 minutes and the Sora 70 at five hours set the high end. We discounted for battery fade.

howWeEvaluated.title: Navigation tech
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared camera, ultrasonic and sensor navigation. Complex pools favour the AquaSense 2 Ultra, simpler ones the Sora 10. We kept the reasoning tied to pool layout.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership promises
howWeEvaluated.description: We read warranty and retrieval features, like the AquaSense 2 protection plan. We looked for caddies and surface parking. For the Beatbot lineup we leaned on the listed battery, charging and surface-coverage specs plus recurring owner remarks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value inside the family
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked each model by how much unique capability it adds over the Sora 10. A feature you cannot use is wasted money. The Sora 10 stays the baseline.

howToChoose.note: Check the listing for current pricing; tiers shift.

cards.label: Camera (AquaSense 2 Ultra)
cards.text: Maps the pool and recognises plant debris, which helps on complex layouts. It needs a clear lens and reasonably clear water. It costs more.

cards.label: Sensors (Sora 10, Sora 30)
cards.text: Ultrasonic sensing is forgiving and works in cloudy water. It lacks the mapping detail of a camera. Suited to simpler pools.

howToChoose.note: Complex pool, pick the Ultra. Everyone else, the Sora models do the job.

rows: Ten thousand mAh and five hours

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for surface skimming and a large basket. Debris that floats for hours needs catching before it sinks. A fine filter will clog quickly, so prefer coarse baskets.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Sora 70 is the only one with surface jets. If a skimming robot is too costly, the Sora 10 with frequent basket rinses is the fallback.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a platform, floating debris or a complex pool. Sora 30, Sora 70 and AquaSense 2 Ultra each solve one of those problems. Pay for the problem you have, and let the rest of the family sit on the shelf.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your pool is a plain deep rectangle. The Sora 10 is enough, and the savings buy spare filters. The extras do nothing for a simple pool.

maintenance.why: Dirt that dries in the mesh is hard to remove. A clogged basket drops suction.
Sunscreen film confuses ultrasonic and vision sensing. A wipe restores accuracy.
Lithium cells dislike heat and deep discharge. Charging promptly keeps capacity.
Blocked jets weaken skimming. A quick clear keeps flow.
Worn rollers lose grip. Replace before they scuff liners.

faq.q: Which Beatbot should most people buy?
faq.a: The Sora 10 suits most in-ground pools because it pairs a long battery with waterline cleaning. Step up only for a specific need. Extras you do not use are wasted.
Only if floating debris is your problem. The Sora 70 skims with JetPulse, but floor robots cannot. Without trees nearby, skip it.

faq.q: Do the cameras work in cloudy water?
faq.a: Vision degrades when water clouds, so keep the pool balanced. Ultrasonic sensing on the Sora models copes better. Water clarity matters.

faq.q: How long will the battery last?
faq.a: Expect strong performance for the first seasons, then gradual fade. Heat accelerates it. Treat stated minutes as new-battery numbers.

faq.q: Does a higher GPH mean cleaner water?
faq.a: No. The number rates pump flow, not debris removal. Intake shape, brush contact and a clean filter matter as much.

faq.q: What does the three-year protection cover?
faq.a: The AquaSense 2 listing mentions full machine replacement. Read the terms, since conditions apply. Register early and keep proof of purchase.
